quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Reason
quests.contextSentence: The election results shocked pollsters, ___ every major survey had predicted a comfortable win for the incumbent.
quests.completedSentence: The election results shocked pollsters, because every major survey had predicted a comfortable win for the incumbent.
quests.ruleExplanation: The wrong predictions are the explanation for the shock, which is what 'because' introduces. 'So' would need the surveys mentioned first as the cause; 'although' would require an actual contradiction, but there isn't one here — the surveys and the shock agree perfectly.
quests.nativeTip: Look at the order of ideas: is the second clause explaining the shock, describing a result of it, or contradicting it?

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Result
quests.contextSentence: Ridership dropped for the third straight month, ___ the transit authority is now considering fare cuts to win riders back.
quests.completedSentence: Ridership dropped for the third straight month, so the transit authority is now considering fare cuts to win riders back.
quests.ruleExplanation: The dropping ridership is stated first as the cause, and 'so' introduces the resulting decision. 'Because' would wrongly reverse that order, and 'although' would require a contradiction that isn't present.
quests.nativeTip: The drop is mentioned first as the cause — check which word correctly introduces what came after it.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: The reviewers praised the film's visuals, ___ they were harshly critical of its pacing and dialogue.
quests.completedSentence: The reviewers praised the film's visuals, although they were harshly critical of its pacing and dialogue.
quests.ruleExplanation: Praise and harsh criticism sit in real tension here, which is what 'although' is built to express. 'Because' and 'so' would both require a cause-and-effect link between the visuals and the pacing, but no such link exists.
quests.nativeTip: Check whether the second half is explaining, resulting from, or pushing back against the first half.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Condition
quests.contextSentence: ___ the quarterly numbers come in below forecast, the board has already prepared a contingency plan.
quests.completedSentence: If the quarterly numbers come in below forecast, the board has already prepared a contingency plan.
quests.ruleExplanation: Missing the forecast is still an open, uncertain possibility, which 'if' introduces. 'When' would wrongly treat it as a certainty, and 'unless' would flip the meaning, suggesting the plan activates only when the numbers don't come in low.
quests.nativeTip: Is a low quarter a sure thing, something the plan only kicks in without, or just one open possibility?

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Condition
quests.contextSentence: The alarm won't disarm ___ you enter the correct code within thirty seconds.
quests.completedSentence: The alarm won't disarm unless you enter the correct code within thirty seconds.
quests.ruleExplanation: The disarming fails without that one positive action, which is exactly the negative-condition logic 'unless' captures. 'If' would need the clause rephrased as a negative ('if you don't enter'), and 'when' would wrongly suggest the code entry is a certainty rather than a requirement.
quests.nativeTip: The alarm stays armed except for one specific positive action — figure out which word matches that structure.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: The fireworks always start ___ the sun fully sets, rain or shine.
quests.completedSentence: The fireworks always start when the sun fully sets, rain or shine.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Always' and 'rain or shine' confirm this is a certain, recurring trigger, not a possibility, which rules out 'if'. 'Unless' makes no sense here since nothing is being excluded.
quests.nativeTip: The phrase 'always' and 'rain or shine' tell you this isn't a maybe — it's a sure, repeating event.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: The witness kept glancing at the door ___ she answered the prosecutor's questions.
quests.completedSentence: The witness kept glancing at the door while she answered the prosecutor's questions.
quests.ruleExplanation: The repeated glancing overlapped with the whole stretch of questioning, which is exactly what 'while' expresses. 'When' would wrongly suggest a single instant, and 'as' risks reading as a reason here rather than simultaneous time.
quests.nativeTip: The glancing happened repeatedly, stretched across the whole time she was talking — not at one single instant.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Time
quests.contextSentence: The power flickered ___ the storm's first lightning strike hit the transformer.
quests.completedSentence: The power flickered when the storm's first lightning strike hit the transformer.
quests.ruleExplanation: The flicker happened at the precise instant of the strike, a single trigger point, which 'when' captures. 'While' would wrongly suggest an ongoing overlap for what is really a one-time event.
quests.nativeTip: The flicker was one sharp, single event tied to one exact strike, not a stretch of overlapping time.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Reason
quests.contextSentence: ___ the deadline was already tight, the manager decided not to add any new requirements.
quests.completedSentence: As the deadline was already tight, the manager decided not to add any new requirements.
quests.ruleExplanation: The tight deadline is the light, background reason behind the decision, which 'as' introduces here. 'When' doesn't fit since the deadline being tight isn't a single triggering moment, and 'while' would misleadingly suggest a comparison or overlap rather than a reason.
quests.nativeTip: The tight deadline is quietly explaining the decision, not describing something happening alongside it.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: ___ the results had already been peer-reviewed twice, the journal still requested a third independent review.
quests.completedSentence: Even though the results had already been peer-reviewed twice, the journal still requested a third independent review.
quests.ruleExplanation: The two completed reviews are an established fact, and 'even though' introduces a concession about that fact. 'Even if' would wrongly treat the review status as still uncertain, and 'because' would nonsensically claim the reviews caused the request for a third one.
quests.nativeTip: The two earlier reviews already happened — this is a settled fact, not a maybe still being considered.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: ___ the pilot fails initial safety checks, engineers plan to retest the modified design within a week.
quests.completedSentence: Even if the pilot fails initial safety checks, engineers plan to retest the modified design within a week.
quests.ruleExplanation: The failure is still an unknown future possibility, which 'even if' introduces as a hypothetical concession. 'Even though' would wrongly claim the failure has already happened, and 'because' doesn't fit since there's no direct cause-and-effect link intended here.
quests.nativeTip: Whether the pilot fails is still completely unknown — this hasn't happened yet.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: The revenue targets were missed again this quarter, ___ leadership remains confident about next year's guidance.
quests.completedSentence: The revenue targets were missed again this quarter, even though leadership remains confident about next year's guidance.
quests.ruleExplanation: The missed targets are a completed, real event, which 'even though' introduces as the fact behind this concession. 'Even if' would wrongly suggest the miss hasn't actually happened, and 'because' would illogically claim the miss is causing the confidence.
quests.nativeTip: The missed targets already happened — this is a done fact the confidence is standing up against.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Reason
quests.contextSentence: ___ the quarterly report had already circulated to all board members beforehand, the CFO skipped a detailed walkthrough during the meeting.
quests.completedSentence: Since the quarterly report had already circulated to all board members beforehand, the CFO skipped a detailed walkthrough during the meeting.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Already circulated beforehand' frames this as accepted background context rather than new information, which is exactly the role 'since' plays. 'Because' would present it as the sentence's central point, which doesn't match this backgrounded framing.
quests.nativeTip: The phrase 'already circulated... beforehand' marks this as known background, not fresh news.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Reason
quests.contextSentence: The intern's badge failed at the security gate ___ IT had not yet added her to the new access system.
quests.completedSentence: The intern's badge failed at the security gate because IT had not yet added her to the new access system.
quests.ruleExplanation: This is presented as newly discovered, central information explaining the failure, which is exactly the direct role 'because' plays. 'Since' would sound odd here because it typically frames already-known background, not a fresh discovery like this one.
quests.nativeTip: This explanation is the actual news of the sentence — the reader is finding this out for the first time.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Reason
quests.contextSentence: ___ the summit's opening session ran long, organizers trimmed ten minutes from every afternoon panel.
quests.completedSentence: As the summit's opening session ran long, organizers trimmed ten minutes from every afternoon panel.
quests.ruleExplanation: This minor operational adjustment fits the light, low-emphasis register of 'as' better than the heavier 'because' or the more substantial background framing of 'since'.
quests.nativeTip: This is a small, routine scheduling adjustment, not a heavily emphasized reason.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Comparison
quests.contextSentence: ___ the west campus relies almost entirely on solar power, the east campus still depends heavily on the municipal grid.
quests.completedSentence: Whereas the west campus relies almost entirely on solar power, the east campus still depends heavily on the municipal grid.
quests.ruleExplanation: Opening a sentence with a comparison between two facts calls for a subordinating word, and 'whereas' is built to start a sentence this way, unlike the coordinating 'but', which cannot open a sentence like this.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence needs to open with the comparison, which only one of these words can naturally do here.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Contrast
quests.contextSentence: The city council approved the budget unanimously, ___ several residents voiced strong objections during the same meeting.
quests.completedSentence: The city council approved the budget unanimously, but several residents voiced strong objections during the same meeting.
quests.ruleExplanation: The word 'unanimously' sets up a strong expectation of agreement, making the objections a real surprise, which 'but' captures better than a plain side-by-side comparison word.
quests.nativeTip: A unanimous vote makes the pushback that follows feel like a genuine surprise, not just a side-by-side comparison.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Comparison
quests.contextSentence: Junior researchers are required to submit quarterly progress reports, ___ senior researchers submit findings only at the end of each project.
quests.completedSentence: Junior researchers are required to submit quarterly progress reports, whereas senior researchers submit findings only at the end of each project.
quests.ruleExplanation: The parallel phrasing describing two policies for two staff groups reads like a formal document, which fits the precise comparison role of 'whereas' rather than the more surprise-driven 'but'.
quests.nativeTip: This reads like formal institutional policy comparing two staff tiers, not a moment of surprise.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Reason
quests.contextSentence: The airline rebooked every affected passenger within the hour ___ the cancellation had already triggered a wave of complaints on social media.
quests.completedSentence: The airline rebooked every affected passenger within the hour because the cancellation had already triggered a wave of complaints on social media.
quests.ruleExplanation: The already-existing complaints are the reason for the fast rebooking, which 'because' introduces even in second position. 'So that' would wrongly imply a future goal, but the complaints are described as already having happened.
quests.nativeTip: The complaints already happened before the rebooking — check which word fits that order as an explanation.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Result
quests.contextSentence: The cancellation triggered a wave of angry posts, ___ the airline rebooked every affected passenger within the hour.
quests.completedSentence: The cancellation triggered a wave of angry posts, so the airline rebooked every affected passenger within the hour.
quests.ruleExplanation: The angry posts are stated first as the cause, and 'so' introduces the airline's reactive response that followed. 'So that' would wrongly frame this as a forward-looking goal rather than an already-happening reaction.
quests.nativeTip: The posts are mentioned first as the cause — check which word introduces what actually followed.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Purpose
quests.contextSentence: The airline streamlined its rebooking process ___ future disruptions wouldn't trigger the same backlash.
quests.completedSentence: The airline streamlined its rebooking process so that future disruptions wouldn't trigger the same backlash.
quests.ruleExplanation: The word 'wouldn't' marks this as a forward-looking intended goal, which 'so that' introduces. 'So' and 'because' would both treat this as an already-settled fact rather than a hoped-for future purpose.
quests.nativeTip: The word 'wouldn't' signals a hoped-for future outcome, not something that has already happened.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Condition
quests.contextSentence: The food truck will stay parked at the stadium later than usual ___ the game runs into overtime.
quests.completedSentence: The food truck will stay parked at the stadium later than usual if the game runs into overtime.
quests.ruleExplanation: Staying later genuinely depends on overtime actually happening, a true dependency, which 'if' introduces. 'Unless' would reverse the meaning entirely, and 'even if' would wrongly suggest the outcome doesn't depend on overtime at all.
quests.nativeTip: The later hours genuinely depend on this one thing actually happening, not on it failing to happen.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Condition
quests.contextSentence: The clinic won't extend its hours ___ demand justifies the extra staffing costs.
quests.completedSentence: The clinic won't extend its hours unless demand justifies the extra staffing costs.
quests.ruleExplanation: The hours stay unchanged unless this one condition is met, which is the negative-condition logic 'unless' expresses. 'If' would need the clause rephrased as a negative to keep the same meaning.
quests.nativeTip: The normal hours hold firm except for one specific thing that would need to happen first.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: The clinic plans to extend its hours for the holiday season, ___ demand ends up lower than projected.
quests.completedSentence: The clinic plans to extend its hours for the holiday season, even if demand ends up lower than projected.
quests.ruleExplanation: The extension plan holds regardless of whether demand ends up low, which 'even if' shows as that unaffected outcome. 'If' would wrongly suggest the plan actually depends on low demand, the opposite of what's intended.
quests.nativeTip: The plan stays fixed no matter which way that future possibility actually goes.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Alternatives
quests.contextSentence: You're welcome to bring ___ a dessert or a side dish — whatever's easier for you.
quests.completedSentence: You're welcome to bring either a dessert or a side dish — whatever's easier for you.
quests.ruleExplanation: This is a plain, friendly offer of two options, which is exactly what 'either... or' expresses. 'Whether' would sound like uncertainty rather than an invitation, and 'neither' would wrongly deny both options.
quests.nativeTip: This is a friendly invitation offering two real options, not an expression of doubt.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Alternatives
quests.contextSentence: I honestly can't tell ___ she's joking or completely serious right now.
quests.completedSentence: I honestly can't tell whether she's joking or completely serious right now.
quests.ruleExplanation: Not being able to tell which of two things is true is a classic case for 'whether', which expresses that uncertainty. 'Either' would sound like offering a choice rather than admitting confusion.
quests.nativeTip: This expresses genuine confusion between two possibilities, not an offer to choose one.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Correlative Conjunctions — Paired Negation
quests.contextSentence: ___ the printer nor the scanner has worked properly since the power outage.
quests.completedSentence: Neither the printer nor the scanner has worked properly since the power outage.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Nor' only ever completes a pair that starts with 'neither', confirming both machines are broken together. 'Either' would need 'or', not 'nor', to complete its pair.
quests.nativeTip: Both machines are broken here, and 'nor' later in the sentence has already chosen its one required partner.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Coordinating Conjunctions — Result
quests.contextSentence: The quarterly forecast missed the mark for the second year running, ___ the CFO is under mounting pressure to explain the gap to shareholders.
quests.completedSentence: The quarterly forecast missed the mark for the second year running, so the CFO is under mounting pressure to explain the gap to shareholders.
quests.ruleExplanation: The missed forecast is the cause, and the mounting pressure is what followed from it, which 'so' introduces. 'Because' would wrongly reverse that direction.
quests.nativeTip: The missed forecast is the cause; check which word introduces the pressure that followed from it.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Concession
quests.contextSentence: ___ the new hire had zero experience in the industry, she outperformed every benchmark within her first quarter.
quests.completedSentence: Although the new hire had zero experience in the industry, she outperformed every benchmark within her first quarter.
quests.ruleExplanation: No prior experience makes outperforming every benchmark genuinely surprising, which 'although' introduces as that concession. 'Because' would nonsensically claim the lack of experience caused the strong results.
quests.nativeTip: Zero experience should have meant a slow start — check whether that's actually what happened.

quests.conceptTitle: Traffic Lights of Logic: Subordinating Conjunctions — Condition
quests.contextSentence: The negotiations remain fragile, ___ either side walks away entirely, which now seems increasingly likely.
quests.completedSentence: The negotiations remain fragile, unless either side walks away entirely, which now seems increasingly likely.
quests.ruleExplanation: The fragile status depends on a full walkaway not happening, and 'unless' introduces that negative condition, especially with 'increasingly likely' signaling real risk. 'Even if' would wrongly suggest the fragile status continues no matter what, contradicting that real risk.
quests.nativeTip: The fragile status only holds up as long as one particular worst-case outcome doesn't happen — and that outcome now looks close.
